headline_finding: STRONG + HONEST. Harness sound: CONTROL mean_rank=0.521 (≈0.5), coverage=0.934 (≈ nominal 0.95). PLUGIN is genuinely MISCALIBRATED under real item noise: KS=0.123 (≫ CONTROL 0.048, strongly rejects uniform), mean_rank=0.574 (biased — posterior below θ*), coverage=0.884 (under-covers). UNCERT RESTORES calibration to the CONTROL baseline: KS=0.031 (uniform NOT rejected), mean_rank=0.509, coverage=0.932. ⇒ propagating the κ-calibrated s_sd is NOT cosmetic; it materially recovers the posterior calibration the plug-in engine LOSES under realistic item-signal noise.
interpretation: θ* drawn from the engine's OWN prior ⇒ any deviation from rank-uniformity is LIKELIHOOD misspecification, not a prior mismatch. CONTROL (no item noise, plug-in) validates the harness via practical calibration (mean_rank≈0.5, coverage≈nominal); see control_ks_note for the KS nuance. PLUGIN ignores real item noise ⇒ overconfident (coverage < 0.95, KS strongly rejects, ranks biased high). UNCERT marginalises the κ-calibrated s_sd ⇒ calibration restored to the CONTROL baseline. Honest directional claim (gated): UNCERT coverage ≥ PLUGIN and UNCERT KS ≤ PLUGIN.
control_ks_note: CONTROL KS (0.0478) marginally exceeds the 0.05 critical value (0.0453) at n=900. This is NOT a harness bug (mean_rank≈0.5, coverage≈nominal prove soundness) and NOT the Phase-3.5 effect: it is the engine SMC's KNOWN finite-particle approximation error, which KS is over-powered to detect at large SBC n even under a correctly-specified likelihood. It is the SHARED baseline of all three arms. The Phase-3.5 claim is the CONTRAST: PLUGIN degrades FAR beyond this baseline (KS 0.123 vs 0.048; cov 0.884 vs 0.934), and UNCERT returns TO the baseline — a contrast that is unambiguous regardless of the absolute KS hard-test.
